campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 1, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered authorizing an agreement with the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority (VTA) to accept low-carbon transportation program funding for a transit reliability and performance improvement project. The agenda also referenced pothole damage claims processes.
keyTopics: Resolution to authorize a low-carbon transportation and operations program fund agreement with VTA
Transit reliability improvement and performance systems project
Pothole damage claims process

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 2, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council reviewed routine business including meeting minutes, check registers, and the Treasurer's Report, along with draft responses to two county grand jury reports on pothole claims and BART/VTA oversight. The Council also considered a transportation impact fee study contract, support for a state data-transparency bill, formation of a committee on alternative policing services, and discussions on the future of the Blossom Festival and Saratoga's involvement in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County.
keyTopics: Draft responses to Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole claims processing and VTA's oversight of BART Silicon Valley Phase II
Support for AB 1761, a bill on data transparency for utility rate calculations
$85,000 contract with Fehr and Peers for a Transportation Impact Fee study
Forming an Ad-Hoc Committee to review alternative policing services in Saratoga
Discussion on the future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival and continued participation in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 8, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council considered several routine administrative and budget items, including updated employee pay schedules and a contract increase for electrical maintenance services. The Council also took up renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street, discussed the future of the Environmental Commission, and reviewed a citizen initiative on potential zoning impacts.
keyTopics: Revised Fiscal Year 2026/27 pay schedules for city employee associations and unrepresented staff
$250,000 increase to the maintenance services agreement with Bear Electrical Solutions
Renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street
Citizen initiative presentation on potential impacts to zoning
Discussion of the Environmental Commission and possible formation of a Council subcommittee

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 1, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council met to approve routine meeting minutes and consider a handful of administrative items, including vacating a public service easement on Cerro Vista, setting up preferential and time-limited parking in certain areas, and hiring a consultant to help with an executive search or related work.
keyTopics: Vacating a public service easement at 15995 Cerro Vista
Establishing preferential permit parking and time-limited parking
Authorizing a consultant agreement for executive-related services
Approval of minutes from several recent Council meetings

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 2, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole met to plan upcoming City Council schedules, canceling the September 8, 2026 meeting and reviewing the draft agenda for September 15, 2026. The committee also considered the City Clerk's public record log for late August and took up a study session on financing tools that could support economic development infrastructure projects.
keyTopics: Cancellation of the September 8, 2026 Council meeting
Review and possible additions to the September 15, 2026 draft agenda
Public record log covering August 20–27, 2026
Study session on infrastructure financing tools for economic development

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Council Neighborhoods Committee — September 10, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View Council Neighborhoods Committee met with city staff on hand to field questions from residents about neighborhood issues. Residents had the option to submit their questions ahead of time through an online form.
keyTopics: City staff attended to answer resident questions about neighborhood matters
Residents were invited to submit questions in advance via an online form

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a special meeting that began with a closed session and was followed by a public presentation. The evening session focused on an update regarding the CleanWater Program.
keyTopics: Closed session held during the 4:30 p.m. special meeting
CleanWater Program update presentation at the 6 p.m. special meeting

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — September 9, 2026
cupertino.summary: Cupertino's Teen Commission kicked off its 2026-2028 term with new commissioners being sworn in and an orientation session for the group. The meeting also included a presentation on teen programs and approval of minutes from the August 12 meeting.
keyTopics: Swearing-in ceremony for incoming 2026-2028 Teen Commissioners
Teen Commission orientation for new members
Presentation on teen programs
Approval of August 12, 2026 meeting minutes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting was held in a hybrid format, allowing both in-person attendance and remote participation via Zoom or phone. One council member, Boardmember Chahal, joined remotely from India. The provided agenda excerpt does not include details on specific policy items or discussion topics beyond meeting logistics.
keyTopics: Hybrid meeting format with in-person and remote (Zoom/phone) participation options for the public
Boardmember Chahal participated remotely from Panchkula, India

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 1, 2026
milpitas.summary: This meeting was held in the city's role as the Successor Agency to the former Redevelopment Agency, handling administrative and financial matters left over from redevelopment. The City Council considered confirming which city officials serve as officers of the Successor Agency, and considered authorizing the sale and issuance of bonds to refinance existing redevelopment-related debt.
keyTopics: Confirming and designating city officials as officers of the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency
Authorizing the sale and issuance of 2026 Tax Allocation Refunding Bonds to refinance Successor Agency debt

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee — September 4, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Climate Action and Sustainability Committee took a preliminary look at Palo Alto's 2025 greenhouse gas inventory, including an overview of Scope 3 emissions (indirect emissions from things like purchased goods and supply chains). The committee also reviewed different approaches the city could take toward its carbon neutrality goal and gave staff feedback on which areas need further analysis.
keyTopics: Preliminary review of the 2025 Greenhouse Gas Inventory and Scope 3 emissions overview
Overview of approaches to achieving the city's carbon neutrality goal, with committee feedback on areas for further staff analysis
Both items determined not to be a project under CEQA
Staff comments and committee member comments and announcements
